explanation: In the US, the thumbs-up is a universally understood positive gesture meaning approval, agreement, or 'all good,' used casually among friends, coworkers, and strangers alike (e.g., signaling OK to a driver). It carries no negative connotation in any American context and is just as common online as in person.
local_tip: Use it freely in casual and most professional settings; it is rarely if ever misread negatively in the US.

also_check.note: Traditionally read as a vulgar insult roughly equivalent to an obscene gesture, not as approval.
Can be used to mean the number 'one' when counting, so context determines whether it reads as approval or a numeral.
Understood the same way as in the US, as a casual sign of approval, with no negative connotation.
